text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"San Diego, CA","level":"city","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Just Cause for Termination of Tenancy)","requirement":"A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. At-fault causes include non-payment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, refusal to sign a substantially similar lease renewal, criminal activity or criminal threat, unlawful sublet, refusal of lawful entry, unlawful use, failure to vacate after employment ends, and failure to deliver possession after the tenant's own notice. No-fault causes, which must be in good faith, are owner or family move-in (minimum 12 continuous months, with the occupant moving in within 90 days), withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court vacate order or local ordinance, and demolition or substantial remodel. Termination notices must state the cause. No-fault notices must be given 30 or 60 days ahead under Civ. Code § 1946.1, in at least 12-point font, and must state the relocation assistance and the right to an offer to re-rent. Relocation assistance for no-fault terminations is paid regardless of tenant income or length of tenancy, by direct payment (due within 15 days of the notice) or rent waiver, at the landlord's option. The landlord must notify the San Diego Housing Commission within three business days. If the unit is re-offered for rent within five years after a no-fault eviction for owner move-in, government-ordered vacate, or demolition/remodel, the landlord must first offer it to the displaced tenant, who has 30 days to accept. Buyout agreements are regulated and void if they are for less than the relocation assistance.
